sentences.text: Respondent :- Dharmpal Singh And Another Counsel for Appellant :- Satya Deo Ojha,Sushil Kumar Pandey Counsel for Respondent :- Aditya Singh Parihar,Atul Kumar Kushwaha Hon'ble Vipin Chandra Dixit,J.

1. Heard Sri Satya Deo Ojha, learned counsel appearing on behalf of appellant, Sri Aditya Singh Parihar, learned counsel appearing on behalf of respondent no. 2 Insurance Company and perused the record.
No one is present on behalf of respondent no. 1, who is owner of the vehicle.

2. This first appeal from order under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act 1988 has been filed on behalf of appellant for enhancement of compensation against the judgment and award dated 3.2.2010 passed by Presiding Officer, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / Additional District Judge,
Court No. 1, Muzaffar Nagar in Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 141 of 2008 (Arvind Giri Versus Dharam Pal Singh and another) by which compensation of Rs. 2,30,000/- along with 6% interest,
has been awarded in favour of claimants / appellants and the liability has been fixed upon respondent no. 2.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for appellants that the parties have amicably settled their dispute outside the Court and the respondent Insurance Company is ready to pay Rs. 8,00,000/- as full and final settlement, which is accepted by the claimants-appellants.
4. A written settlement / compromise, dated 2.10.2024 duly signed by learned counsels for claimants-appellants and Insurance Company has been produced before this Court, which is taken on record.
5. In view of above, this First Appeal From Order is party allowed in terms of compromise.

The claimants-appellants are entitled to get Rs. 8,00,000/- as full and final settlement towards their claim, apart from the amount, which had already been received by them in compliance of the award dated 3.2.2010 passed in Motor Accident Claim Petition No. 141 of 2008 (Arvind Giri Versus Dharam Pal Singh and another).
6. The respondent no. 2 Insurance Company is directed to pay the agreed amount within a period of sixty days, failing which, claimants-appellants are entitled for 6% interest on the agreed amount.
